7856.q: Why does the robin defend its territory in winter too?
a: So that it has enough food for itself
Because it is afraid of snow
Because it wants to sing loudest then
7856.e: Even in winter the robin needs its own area with enough food. That is why it defends its territory all year round.
7856.m: It defends its territory in winter.

7857.q: Can a roe deer swim well?
a: Yes, roe deer can swim well
No, roe deer cannot swim at all
Roe deer live only in water
7857.e: Even if you might not think so at first, roe deer can swim well. They use this, for example, to cross a river.
7857.m: Roe deer are surprisingly good swimmers.

7858.q: What helps the European pond turtle survive better in its habitat?
a: New ponds and sunny places to lay eggs
More concrete walls by the water
7858.e: Conservationists create ponds and open, sandy spots for egg pits. Sometimes young turtles are also raised and released into the wild.
7858.m: New ponds and egg-laying sites help.

7859.q: Which large group of animals does the European garden spider belong to?
7859.e: The garden spider, like all other spiders, belongs to the arachnids. Animals in this group have eight legs and no antennae.

7860.q: Roughly what does a dung beetle larva look like?
a: Fat, pale and curved into a C shape
Long and thin like a wire
Green and flat like a leaf
7860.e: Larvae like this are called grubs. They usually lie curled up in the soil.
7860.m: The larva is a curled-up grub.

7861.q: Do rhinos usually live alone or in large groups?
a: Always in huge herds of a hundred animals
Always in twos like a pair
Always in family groups of twenty animals
7861.e: Adult rhinos usually live alone, except for mothers with their young. Only sometimes are they found in small groups.

7862.q: In which month are most ibex kids born?
7862.e: Most kids are born in June, when there is already enough fresh food in the mountains. The mother looks for a sheltered rock ledge for the birth.
7862.m: Ibex kids are born in June.

7863.q: In the dish “trout au bleu”, the trout's skin turns bluish. Where does this colour come from?
a: The layer of slime reacts with vinegar
The trout is dyed with food colouring
7863.e: The trout is cooked fresh, with its layer of slime, in a vinegar stock. This turns the skin bluish.
7863.m: Vinegar turns the slime layer blue.

7864.q: What is the effect called when white light is split into its colours in a prism?
7864.e: In dispersion, different wavelengths of light are refracted by different amounts. That is why a visible colour spectrum appears when light passes through a prism.

7865.q: Do earwigs really like crawling into human ears?
a: Yes, they lay their eggs there
Yes, they look for the warmth in the ear on purpose
7865.e: If an earwig gets into an ear, it is by chance, and it hardly ever happens. It prefers narrow cracks that are dark and sheltered.
7865.m: Earwigs do not seek out ears on purpose.

7866.q: Which group of animals does the European pond turtle belong to?
7866.e: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin or horny plates and usually lay eggs on land. Snakes and lizards belong to this group too.
7866.m: Turtles are reptiles with a horny shell.

7867.q: Why is its flat body useful for the earwig?
a: It lets it fit into narrow cracks
7867.e: Thanks to its flat body, it can slip into narrow gaps under bark and stones. There it is well hidden.
7867.m: A flat body fits into narrow hiding places.

7868.q: How many different fins does a goldfish normally have?
a: Several, for example dorsal, pelvic, pectoral and tail fins
7868.e: A goldfish has several different fins that help it swim, steer and brake. These include, for example, the dorsal fin and the tail fin.

7869.q: What do we drink that comes from the cow?
7869.e: Cows give milk, which you can drink or make into cheese and yoghurt. That is why there are many dairy cows on farms.

7870.q: What does the aardwolf mainly eat?
7870.e: The aardwolf belongs to the hyena family, but it mainly eats termites. It licks them up with its sticky tongue.

7871.q: What is the stage called when the larva leaves the water and becomes a dragonfly?
7871.e: The larva climbs out of the water up a plant stem. Then its skin splits open and the adult dragonfly emerges.
7871.m: The dragonfly emerges from the larva's skin.

7872.q: How does the koala manage to climb trees so well?
a: With strong arms, claws and gripping paws
7872.e: The koala has strong arms, sharp claws and special gripping paws with thumbs. With them it can hold on safely to branches and climb up.
7872.m: Strong arms and claws help with climbing.

7873.q: What colour is the wels catfish usually on its back?
7873.e: The back is usually dark, often with a marbled pattern. The belly is paler.

7874.q: Which family of mammals does the puma belong to?
7874.e: The puma belongs to the cat family. Within it, it counts as one of the small cats, even though it grows quite large.

7875.q: What role does the sand lizard play in the ecosystem?
a: It eats lots of insects and is itself food for other animals
It cleans algae out of ponds
7875.e: As a predator of insects and as prey for birds and other animals, it is an important link in the food chain. If it disappeared, it would affect other species.
7875.m: It is hunter and prey at the same time.

7876.q: What colour is the skin of the blue whale usually?
7876.e: The blue whale's skin is actually rather grey, but in the water it often looks bluish. That is where its name comes from.
7876.m: In the water it shimmers bluish.

7877.q: Do other animals reuse old woodpecker holes?
7877.e: When the woodpecker moves out, other animals such as tits or bats often move in. So the hole stays useful for a long time.

7878.q: Roughly how long are eagle owl eggs incubated before the chicks hatch?
7878.e: Eagle owl eggs are incubated for about 34 days before the chicks hatch. After that it still takes many weeks until the young birds can fly.
7878.m: Eagle owl eggs are incubated for about 34 days.

7879.q: What do pike eggs stick to?
7879.e: The sticky eggs of the pike cling to water plants. There they are better protected than in open water.
7879.m: Pike eggs stick to water plants.

a: No, but it is very skilled at flying sideways and turning
Yes, just as well as forwards
Yes, but only very slowly straight backwards
7880.e: A housefly cannot really fly backwards. But it is an expert at turning quickly and dodging sideways.
7880.m: Flies turn instead of flying backwards.

7881.q: When do swifts usually return to Switzerland from Africa?
a: At the end of April or the beginning of May
In the depths of winter, in December
7881.e: After the long journey from Africa, swifts usually arrive in Switzerland at the end of April. There they move back into their old nesting sites.

7882.q: What is the aim of the Paris Climate Agreement?
7882.e: In the Paris Climate Agreement, almost every country in the world committed to fighting climate change together. Switzerland has also signed the agreement.
7882.m: The Paris Agreement limits global warming.

7884.q: What colour are adult female sand lizards usually?
7884.e: Females usually stay brownish with a row of dark spots on their back. This camouflages them well in dry grass and on soil.
7884.m: Females are usually brown and spotted, not green.

7885.q: Roughly how much does a male red kite weigh?
7885.e: Male red kites weigh just under a kilogram on average. Females are usually a little heavier than males.
7885.m: A male red kite weighs just under a kilo.

7886.q: What do some millipedes release to defend themselves?
7886.e: Many species have defence glands and release foul-smelling substances. Some contain cyanide compounds.

7887.q: Why does a rhinoceros like to roll in mud?
a: To protect itself from the sun and insects
7887.e: The mud dries on the skin and protects the rhino from the hot sun and annoying insects. It is like a natural sun cream.
7887.m: Mud protects the rhino from the sun.

7888.q: Why are sparrows becoming rarer in some big cities?
a: Because there are fewer nesting sites and less food
Because they forget how to fly
Because they can't find friends any more
7888.e: When old houses are renovated, the small holes where sparrows can nest often disappear. Some cities also have fewer insects and green spaces for finding food.

7890.q: How widespread is the eagle owl around the world?
a: It lives in large parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa
It lives only in a small area of Switzerland
It lives only in South America
7890.e: The eagle owl has a very large range covering large parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa. This makes it one of the most widespread owl species of all.
7890.m: Eagle owls live in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

7891.q: In which country outside Africa is there still a small population of lions?
7891.e: A small, protected group of Asiatic lions lives in the Gir Forest in India. It is the last natural home of lions outside Africa.
7891.m: Asiatic lions still live in India.

a: The explosion of a massive star at the end of its life
The birth of a new star from clouds of gas
An especially bright planet in the night sky
A new moon of the Earth
7892.e: When massive stars use up their nuclear fuel, they collapse and explode extremely brightly. For a short time a supernova can shine more brightly than a whole galaxy.
7892.m: A supernova is the explosion of a star at the end of its life.

7893.q: What danger often threatens edible frogs as they migrate between their winter shelter and their breeding pond?
a: Sea water that is too cold
7893.e: On the way to their breeding ponds, edible frogs sometimes have to cross roads, and many get run over. That is why amphibian fences and tunnels are built in some places.

7894.q: What is it called when water turns into water vapour?
7894.e: When water is heated strongly, it turns into invisible water vapour that rises into the air. You know this from a boiling pan.
7894.m: Hot water evaporates into the air.

7895.q: What is a fish trap like the ones used to catch eels?
a: A trap that fish can swim into but not find their way out of
A net thrown from a boat
7895.e: A fish trap is a device that fish can get into but cannot find their way out of. Eel traps are laid on the bottom of the water.
7895.m: Eels are often caught with traps.

7896.q: Are you allowed to simply take wild European pond turtles home?
a: Yes, if you feed them well
7896.e: Wild animals belong in nature, and the European pond turtle is strictly protected. If you find one, it is best to watch it from a distance.
7896.m: Protected wild animals stay in nature.

7897.q: What do male okapis have on their heads?
7897.e: Males have so-called ossicones, small bony knobs covered with skin and fur. Females usually have none.
7897.m: Only male okapis have short little horns.

7898.q: What does a giraffe's coat usually look like?
7898.e: A giraffe's coat is usually light yellowish brown with large dark patches. This pattern also helps it hide in the shade of trees.
7898.m: Giraffes have yellowish brown coats with patches.

7899.q: What does a tiger have under its paws so that it can walk very quietly?
7899.e: A tiger's paws have soft pads that let it walk almost silently through the forest. This helps it creep up on prey.

7900.q: What does a bumblebee do with its long tongue?
7900.e: With its long tongue, the bumblebee can reach deep into a flower. That is how it gets to the sweet nectar.
7900.m: The tongue sucks nectar from flowers.

7902.q: Roughly how many species of aphid are there worldwide?
7902.e: Around 5,000 species are known worldwide, with many hundreds in Central Europe. They live mainly in temperate regions.

7903.q: What do African elephants mainly eat?
a: Plants such as grass, leaves and bark
7903.e: Elephants eat only plants. They eat grass, leaves, bark and fruit.

7904.q: Why are alpine newts popular animals for biologists to observe in ponds?
a: Because they are easy to see and live in many waters
Because they are huge and noisy
Because they only live in the jungle at night
7904.e: Alpine newts live in many ponds and are easy to see during the breeding season, so they are easy to observe and study. This makes them a popular species for amphibian counts.
7904.m: Alpine newts are common and easy to observe.

7905.e: Only female chickens, the hens, can lay eggs. The cockerel does not have the body parts needed for it.

a: A year with a particularly large number of cockchafers
A year when cockchafers are banned
A year when cockchafers are white
7906.e: Because cockchafers take several years to develop, they appear in large numbers in certain years. This is called a flight year or cockchafer year.
7906.m: Cockchafer years have lots of beetles.

7907.q: What does a ring-tailed lemur's nose look like?
a: Moist and bare, like a dog's
Flat with no nostrils at all
7907.e: Ring-tailed lemurs have a moist nose tip. They belong to the wet-nosed primates, and the moist nose helps them smell.
7907.m: Ring-tailed lemurs have a moist nose.

7908.q: What clearly sets the common frog apart from the common toad?
a: The common frog has smooth, moist skin
The common frog has warty skin
The common frog has a tail
The common frog has shorter back legs
7908.e: The common toad has warty, dry skin, while the common frog's skin is smooth and moist. This makes the two species easy to tell apart.
7908.m: Frog skin is smooth, toad skin is warty.

7909.q: What does the carp use its barbels for?
a: To feel for food on the bottom
7909.e: In murky water the carp cannot always see well. With its barbels it can feel where food is.
7909.m: Carp feel their food with their barbels.

7910.q: What is special about the Svalbard reindeer?
a: It has no fur at all
7910.e: The Svalbard reindeer is smaller than other reindeer. This helps it save heat.

7911.q: Roughly how old can a common toad get in the wild?
7911.e: Common toads can live for about ten years in the wild, some even longer. That is quite old for a small animal.
7911.m: Common toads often live ten years.

7912.q: How do its big ears help the red deer?
a: It hears danger from far away
It smells its food with them
It keeps its balance with them
It warms itself with them in winter
7912.e: The large, movable ears pick up every little sound. So the deer notices enemies early.

7913.q: Why is a cat also a danger to great tits at the bird feeder?
7913.e: Cats are good hunters and can take birds by surprise, especially when they sit on the ground or at low feeding places. That is why it is better to hang bird feeders higher up.
7913.m: Cats can catch birds at feeding places.

7914.q: How does the tawny owl react when another tawny owl enters its territory?
a: It defends its territory with loud calls and, if necessary, attacks
7914.e: Tawny owls are territorial and actively defend their territory with calls, sometimes even attacking intruders directly. This secures their hunting ground and nesting hole.
7914.m: Tawny owls actively defend their territory.

7915.q: Which bird likes to catch young trout in streams?
7915.e: The grey heron stands still in the water and snaps at lightning speed. Other fish-eaters also hunt small trout.

7916.q: What is the difference between a watt and a watt-hour?
a: A watt is power, a watt-hour is an amount of energy used
A watt only measures heat, a watt-hour only light
A watt-hour measures time, a watt measures weight
7916.e: Watts show how much energy an appliance uses per second. If an appliance runs at this power for one hour, it has used one watt-hour of energy.
7916.m: A watt is power, a watt-hour is energy.

7917.q: Where does a sea trout swim back to when it wants to lay eggs?
a: To the river where it hatched
To a warm lake in the south
To the deepest point in the sea
7917.e: To spawn, the sea trout finds its way back to the river where it hatched itself. There it lays its eggs in the gravel bed.
7917.m: Sea trout return to the river where they were born.

7918.q: Why was hunting the lynx widespread in the past?
a: Because its meat was a delicacy
Because it was popular as a pet
7918.e: The thick, spotted fur of the lynx was highly prized for making furs for a long time. This led to heavy hunting and almost to its extinction in Central Europe.
7918.m: Its fur made the lynx a target.

7919.q: What do we call birds that fly to warmer countries in autumn, like the stork?
7919.e: Birds that fly away in autumn and come back in spring are called migratory birds. The white stork is one of them.

7920.q: What do chickens often do when they are very hot?
a: They lie in the full sun
7920.e: In great heat, chickens look for cool, shady spots. Sometimes they open their beaks to cool down.
7920.m: In the heat, chickens look for shade.

7921.q: Do adult female cheetahs usually live alone or in groups?
7921.e: Female cheetahs usually live alone, except when raising young. Males sometimes form small groups.

7922.q: Does a panda usually move rather slowly or very fast?
a: Always very fast like a cheetah
7922.e: Pandas are easy-going animals that usually move slowly. They spend a lot of time eating and resting.
7922.m: Pandas usually move at a leisurely pace.

7923.q: What does the swift use its sticky saliva for when building its nest?
a: To glue nesting material such as feathers and stalks together
7923.e: As the swift hardly ever lands, it collects nesting material such as feathers and bits of plants directly in the air. With its sticky saliva it glues these pieces into a firm nest.
7923.m: Sticky saliva holds the nest together.

7924.q: Roughly how big can a fully grown blue whale get?
7924.e: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world. It can be as long as three coaches in a row.
7924.m: Blue whales are huge and very long.

7925.q: What do some aphid species do during the year?
a: They change the type of plant they live on
They move to Africa in autumn
They live in water in winter
7925.e: Some species live on one type of plant in summer and on another in winter. This change is called host alternation.
7925.m: Some aphids change host plants during the year.

7926.q: What shape is an eel's body in cross-section?
7926.e: In cross-section, an eel's body is almost round. Only the tail is somewhat flattened at the sides.

7927.q: How are young grey herons fed in the nest?
a: With food brought back up by the parents
With small insects, one at a time in the beak
7927.e: The parents bring up predigested food from their crop. The young then pick this food straight from their parents' beaks.
7927.m: Parents bring food back up for their young.

7929.q: What do the feathers of young peregrine falcons look like compared to adults?
a: More brown instead of bluish grey
7929.e: Young falcons first wear brown juvenile plumage before they get the bluish grey feathers of adults after their first moult. This makes it possible to tell young and old birds apart.
7929.m: Young falcons are brown at first.

7930.q: Where does the great tit like to nest best?
7930.e: Great tits like to breed in holes in old trees. They also happily use nest boxes that people put up.
7930.m: Great tits breed in holes and nest boxes.

7931.q: Why is a trout's body so slim and pointed?
a: So that it can swim quickly through the water
So that it can bury itself in the sand
So that it can go a long time without food
So that it doesn't get cold in winter
7931.e: The trout's slim body helps it move quickly and easily through the water. This way it can also swim against the current.
7931.m: A slim body makes trout fast.

7932.q: What does a bumblebee do before it takes off in the cold?
7932.e: By shivering its flight muscles, the bumblebee makes heat in its body. Only when it is warm enough can it take off.

7933.q: Why do ring-tailed lemurs like to warm up in the sun in the morning?
a: They need warmth after cool nights
They want to bleach their fur white
They can only drink water in daylight
They have to do it to feed their young
7933.e: The nights in Madagascar can be cool. The morning sun helps the animals warm up again.
7933.m: The sun warms lemurs after a cold night.

7934.q: What does a hedgehog build its winter nest from?
7934.e: The hedgehog gathers leaves and grass and builds a warm nest out of them. It spends its whole hibernation safely inside.
7934.m: Hedgehogs build their nest from leaves.

7935.q: How does the wels catfish often spend the day?
a: Hidden in caves or under roots
High above the water on branches
In a shoal at the surface
7935.e: During the day, the wels catfish likes to rest in sheltered spots such as hollows in the bank or dead wood. It only starts hunting in the evening.
7935.m: The wels catfish hides during the day.

7936.q: Which dog breed often helps the shepherd to round up the sheep?
7936.e: Border collies are very clever dogs that help the shepherd gather the sheep into a flock. They can show the sheep exactly where to go.
7936.m: Border collies are skilled at herding sheep.

7937.q: What does the term “herd animal” mean?
a: An animal that lives in a group
An animal that lives in water
An animal that only eats at night
7937.e: Herd animals benefit from protection and sticking together. Cape buffaloes are a good example.

7938.q: How quickly can a newborn calf stand up?
7938.e: A calf can stand on its wobbly legs shortly after birth. After a few hours it is even walking around.

7939.q: Can an octopus change the colour and pattern of its skin?
7939.e: The octopus has tiny colour cells in its skin. With them it can adapt to its surroundings in a flash.

7940.q: Which dog breed is known for its great speed in races?
7940.e: The greyhound, a sighthound, is considered one of the fastest dog breeds in the world and is traditionally used for dog racing. Its slim build is designed for speed.
7940.m: The greyhound is a very fast dog.

7941.q: What happens to the colony when a marmot burrow becomes too small for everyone?
a: Some animals dig new burrows nearby
The whole colony dies out immediately
All the animals move down to the valley
They build nests in trees instead
7941.e: When the colony grows, some marmots dig extra burrows in the area. Over time this creates larger burrow systems with several entrances.

7942.q: What does the magpie do when it notices danger?
a: It warns other animals nearby with loud calls
It immediately hides in the ground
It goes completely quiet and doesn't move
7942.e: Magpies are seen as alert guards of their territory and warn of dangers such as predators with loud calls. Other animals in the area often benefit from this warning too.
7942.m: Magpies give loud warnings of danger.

7943.q: How does a brown bear normally move around?
a: It walks on the whole sole of its foot, like a human
Only on tiptoe, like a cat
Only by crawling on its belly
7943.e: Brown bears walk on the soles of their feet and put the whole sole on the ground when walking. This sets them apart from many other predators that walk on their toes.
7943.m: Bears walk on the whole sole of the foot.

7944.q: Which animal is most similar to the alpine salamander in body shape, but differs by having yellow spots?
7944.e: Fire salamanders and alpine salamanders belong to the same genus. The main difference is the colour: the fire salamander has yellow or orange spots on a black background.
7944.m: The fire salamander has yellow spots, the alpine salamander does not.

7945.q: What is the area called where a hyena clan lives and which it defends?
7945.e: Clans defend their territory against other hyenas. They mark it with scent and droppings.

7946.q: What shows that dolphins are also curious about humans?
a: They sometimes come close to boats and swimmers
They flee immediately from every boat
They always hide in deep water
7946.e: Dolphins are naturally curious. They often come close to boats or swimmers to watch them.
7946.m: Dolphins are often curious about people.

7947.q: Why had the otter disappeared from Switzerland for a long time?
a: Because of hunting and polluted waters
Because there were too many fish in the water
7947.e: Heavy hunting and polluted rivers caused numbers to drop sharply. For a long time the otter was therefore considered to have disappeared from Switzerland.
7947.m: Hunting and pollution drove the otter away.

7948.q: What is a capybara, which the jaguar hunts?
7948.e: The capybara is the largest living rodent in the world. It likes to live near water, which makes it prey for the jaguar.

7949.q: What is the common raven among the world's songbirds?
a: The largest songbird in the world
The smallest songbird in the world
The loudest songbird in the world
The rarest songbird in the world
7949.e: Although it doesn't seem like one, the common raven is biologically a songbird. With its size it beats all other species in this group.
7949.m: The largest songbird in the world.

7950.q: By what other name is the stoat also known?
7950.e: The stoat is also called the ermine. Polecats, beech martens and badgers are other species in the weasel family.
7950.m: The stoat is also called the ermine.

7951.q: How does the praying mantis usually move around?
a: Slowly on its four back legs
7951.e: It needs its front legs for catching prey. For walking it uses the other four legs.
7951.m: Walks on four legs, catches with two.

7953.q: Which sense is especially strong in the tawny owl?
7953.e: Thanks to its excellent hearing, the tawny owl can locate prey in complete darkness just by the sounds it makes. Its facial disc guides the sound to its ears.

7954.q: What danger does the destruction of small ponds pose for the alpine newt?
a: It doesn't affect it at all
It simply moves to the sea
7954.e: When pools and ponds are drained or filled in, the alpine newt loses important places to breed. This can endanger whole populations.
7954.m: Lost ponds endanger the alpine newt.

7955.q: What colour do Buddhist monks often wear in many countries?
7955.e: In many Buddhist countries monks wear orange or saffron-coloured robes. This colour has a long tradition.
7955.m: Buddhist monks often wear orange robes.

a: A very well-known award for special achievements
7956.e: The Nobel Prize is awarded every year to people who have achieved great things, for example for peace or science. Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.
7956.m: The Nobel Prize honours special achievements.

7957.q: Where are the barn owl's eyes?
a: At the front of the head
On the sides, like a mouse's
At the back of the head
7957.e: Both of the barn owl's eyes face forwards. This lets it judge distances well.

7958.q: What is it called when several pairs of sparrows nest close together?
7958.e: Sparrows often build their nests close together, which is called a colony. That way they help each other spot enemies early.
7958.m: Many nests together are called a colony.

7959.q: What does a harbour seal's snout look like?
a: Short and round, like a dog's
Long and pointed, like a crocodile's
7959.e: Many people think the harbour seal's short, round snout looks like a dog's head. In German it is even called a “sea dog”.
7959.m: Harbour seals have a round, dog-like snout.

7960.q: How is the barn owl doing in Switzerland?
a: It lives everywhere in huge numbers
It doesn't live there at all
7960.e: There are only a few barn owls left in Switzerland. That is why they are protected and sometimes get special nest boxes.
7960.m: The barn owl is protected in Switzerland.

7961.q: What are the centres called where orphaned orangutans are nursed back to health?
7961.e: There, young animals are cared for and prepared for life in the forest. Later they are meant to be released into the wild.

7962.q: Which category does the okapi have on the Red List?
7962.e: The IUCN classifies the okapi as endangered. Its numbers have fallen.

7963.q: What do adult stag beetles mainly feed on?
7963.e: They lick sap oozing from damaged trees, especially oaks. For this they have a brush-like tongue.
7963.m: Adult stag beetles lick sweet tree sap.

a: A female that collects food and looks after the nest
A strange insect in the nest
7964.e: Worker bumblebees are females that help the queen in summer. They collect nectar and pollen and look after the larvae.
7964.m: Workers collect food for the nest.

7965.q: What do guinea pigs often do together when there is loud thunder outside or something noisy happens?
a: They all run into their hiding place at the same time
They dance together in a circle
They lie motionless in the sun
7965.e: As prey animals, guinea pigs often react to sudden loud noises at lightning speed and run into their hiding place together. This is a natural protective reflex.
7965.m: When it's noisy, guinea pigs flee together.

7966.q: What colours can a starfish be?
7966.e: Starfish come in many colours such as orange, red or blue. Each species has its own colour.

7968.q: What do common toads have behind their eyes that they use for defence?
7968.e: Behind the eyes of the common toad are poison glands called parotoid glands. When in danger, they release a bitter fluid.
7968.m: Poison glands sit behind the eyes.

7970.q: Why do dolphins often swim together in groups?
a: It protects them and helps them hunt
Because they would otherwise get bored
Because they can't breathe on their own
Because the sea is too crowded
7970.e: In a group, dolphins can protect each other and hunt fish together more easily. That is why many dolphins live together.
7970.m: Groups protect them and help them hunt.

7971.q: Which animals sometimes look like millipedes but are insects?
7971.e: Caterpillars are the larvae of butterflies and moths and are therefore insects. Woodlice are crustaceans, earthworms are worms, and centipedes, like millipedes, are myriapods.

7972.q: Roughly how much does an adult common buzzard weigh?
7972.e: An adult common buzzard weighs about 600 grams to 1.3 kilograms, depending on whether it is male or female. Females are usually at the upper end.

7973.q: What are the droppings called that otters use to mark their territory?
7973.e: Spraints are otter droppings, often left in eye-catching places such as stones. They are an important sign for other otters.

7974.q: How does the badger look after itself?
a: It never bathes or cleans itself
7974.e: Badgers like to keep their fur clean and groom themselves regularly. This keeps them healthy.

7975.q: What should you do after an adder bite?
a: Stay calm, keep the body part still, call the emergency number 144
7975.e: Movement speeds up the spread of the venom. You should stay calm and get help immediately.

7976.q: What does a barn owl do when it feels threatened?
7976.e: When a barn owl feels threatened, it hisses and snorts loudly. It wants to chase the attacker away.

7977.q: What do the feathers of a female mallard look like?
7977.e: The female is brown and speckled. This protects her from enemies while sitting on her eggs, because she is hard to see in the grass.

7978.q: Which subspecies of the African buffalo lives mainly in the rainforests of Central Africa?
7978.e: The forest buffalo is smaller and often has reddish fur. It lives in dense forests.
7978.m: The forest buffalo lives in the rainforest.

7979.q: Which mosquitoes bite us humans, males or females?
7979.e: Only female mosquitoes bite, because they need blood for their eggs. Males only drink plant juices.
7979.m: Only female mosquitoes bite and suck blood.

7980.q: How big is a freshly hatched young carp?
7980.e: When a carp hatches from its egg, it is tiny, only a few millimetres long. Only over time does it grow into a big fish.
7980.m: Young carp are tiny at first.

7981.q: How do mallards often react to people in city parks?
a: They are often tame and come closer
They immediately hide deep in the forest
7981.e: In cities, mallards have got used to people. Many even come close when they think there is food.

7982.q: How do dung beetles usually find fresh dung?
a: With their sense of smell, using their antennae
With their big eyes from high up
7982.e: The antennae have many sensory cells for smells. With them the beetles can smell dung from far away.

7983.q: What can develop among aphids when a colony becomes very large and crowded?
a: Winged aphids that fly to new plants
7983.e: When it gets overcrowded or food is poor, winged aphids develop. They fly away and settle on new plants.
7983.m: Winged aphids settle on new plants.

7984.q: What does a jellyfish lack compared to many other animals?
a: A brain, a heart and blood
7984.e: Unlike many animals, a jellyfish has no brain, no heart and no real blood. Even so, it can swim, catch food and reproduce.
7984.m: A jellyfish has no brain, heart or blood.

7985.q: How does a great tit's song differ from its alarm call?
a: The song is more tuneful, the alarm call short and sharp
They always sound exactly the same
Only females sing, males only give warnings
7985.e: The great tit's song is tuneful and used to find a partner. Its alarm call, on the other hand, is short and sharp to warn other birds of danger.
7985.m: Song and alarm call sound completely different.

7986.q: Who sits on the eggs in grey herons?
a: No one, the sun warms them
7986.e: In grey herons, both parents share the job of sitting on the eggs. So one bird always stays at the nest while the other looks for food.

7987.q: Who usually builds the nest in blackbirds?
a: Other birds build it for them
7987.e: It is mainly the female that carefully builds the nest from grass and mud. During this time the male often keeps watch nearby.
7987.m: The female usually builds the nest.

7988.q: What is a male domestic cat called?
7988.e: A male cat is called a tom. The female is called a queen or simply a cat.
7988.m: A tom is a male cat.

7989.q: How do elephants get dust onto their skin?
a: They blow it over their back with their trunk
They let the wind blow it on
7989.e: Elephants suck up dust or sand with their trunk and blow it over their back. This protects their skin from sun and insects.
7989.m: Elephants dust themselves with their trunk.

7990.q: What does the eagle owl do with indigestible remains such as bones and fur after eating?
a: It coughs them up as a pellet
It digests them slowly over several weeks
It hides them in the nest
It passes them on to its young
7990.e: The eagle owl coughs up indigestible parts of its prey such as bones, fur or feathers as a so-called pellet. Such pellets are often found where it rests.
7990.m: Eagle owls cough up remains as pellets.

7991.q: How can you usually recognise the male common earwig?
a: By its more strongly curved pincers
By its two pairs of antennae
7991.e: In the male, the pincers are much more strongly curved. In the female they look straighter.

7992.q: In which Swiss canton were the first captive-bred ibex released back into the wild?
7992.e: In 1911, ibex were released into the wild again for the first time in the Weisstannen valley in the canton of St Gallen. From there the species spread back across the Alps.
7992.m: St Gallen was the first release site.

7993.q: What does the European garden spider do when it feels threatened?
a: It drops down on a thread or plays dead
It jumps at the attacker straight away
7993.e: When in danger, the garden spider sometimes simply drops down on a thread and hides. Sometimes it also stays completely still.

7994.q: How many broods can a pair of kingfishers have per year?
a: Never more than one every two years
7994.e: A pair of kingfishers can raise up to three broods in one year if there is enough food. This helps make up for losses to predators.
7994.m: Up to three broods a year are possible.

7995.q: Apart from the tail, how can you recognise the red kite's wings in flight?
a: By pale patches on the underside of the wings
By completely black wings with no pattern
7995.e: On the underside of its wings, the red kite has striking pale patches called windows. Together with the forked tail, they help identify it.
7995.m: Pale wing windows mark the red kite.

7997.q: What does the elk (moose) do with the food in its stomach after eating?
a: It stores it in its fur
7997.e: Elk are ruminants. They bring food back up from the rumen into the mouth and chew it again.

7998.q: What does a donkey need to feel happy?
a: Space to roam, a second donkey and a dry stable
A small stable all to itself
A blanket and a warm living room
7998.e: Donkeys need lots of exercise, at least one other donkey for company and a dry shelter from the rain. That way they stay healthy and content.

7999.q: Who mainly sits on the eggs in barn swallows?
a: No one, the eggs lie uncovered
7999.e: In barn swallows, it is mainly the female that incubates the eggs. But the male sometimes helps and defends the territory.

8000.q: How do red kite pairs often behave over several years?
a: They often stay together and use the same nest
They never live together as a pair
8000.e: Many red kites stay with the same partner for years and return to the same nest year after year. This is called nest site fidelity.
8000.m: Red kites are often faithful for many years.

8001.q: Why is the common frog one of the most common frog species in Switzerland?
a: Because it can adapt well to different habitats
Because it only lives in zoos
8001.e: The common frog lives in many different habitats, from forests to high up in the mountains. This adaptability makes it one of the most widespread frog species in Switzerland.

8002.q: What does a koala do when it wants to get from one tree to another?
a: It climbs down and walks across the ground
It always jumps more than 50 metres
8002.e: If a koala wants to get to another tree, it usually has to climb down first and walk a little way across the ground. Only then does it climb up a new tree.
8002.m: Koalas walk on the ground to new trees.

8003.q: How does the wels catfish mainly breathe?
a: Through air tubes like an insect
8003.e: Like most fish, it takes oxygen from the water with its gills. Some oxygen can also be taken in through the skin.

8004.q: What do the eggs of the Roman snail look like?
8004.e: Roman snail eggs are small, round and white. They lie in the soil, protected from enemies.
8004.m: Snail eggs are small and white.

8005.q: What colour are a mute swan's legs?
8005.e: A mute swan's legs and feet are black. You can see this well when it comes out of the water.

8006.q: Roughly how old can a rhinoceros get in the wild?
8006.e: In the wild, rhinos can live to about 35 to 40 years. That is quite long for a wild animal.

8007.q: How does a ring-tailed lemur often sit when it sunbathes?
a: Upright, belly facing the sun, with arms spread out
Hanging upside down from a branch
Flat on its back in the water
8007.e: Ring-tailed lemurs like to sit upright and hold their pale belly up to the sun. It looks almost like a person sunbathing.

8009.q: What is the place called where a female wolf gives birth to her pups?
8009.e: For the birth and the pups' first weeks, the she-wolf digs or uses a sheltered den. There the helpless pups are protected from enemies and weather.
8009.m: Pups grow up in a den.

8010.q: What is a female tiger called?
8010.e: A female tiger is called a tigress. The male is simply called a tiger.
8010.m: The female is called a tigress.

8011.q: What danger do fish farms pose to wild salmon?
8011.e: In crowded net pens, parasites such as sea lice multiply quickly. They can spread to wild salmon.
8011.m: Sea lice spread in salmon farming.

8012.q: What does the European garden spider use to build its web?
8012.e: The garden spider makes a sticky liquid in its body. In the air this becomes a fine thread.
8012.m: The spider spins from its own body.

8013.q: When is the slow worm often especially active?
a: Only in the middle of the night in winter
Only in the greatest midday heat
8013.e: That is when the slugs and worms it hunts are out and about. It is also damp, which it likes.
8013.m: Slow worms are often out after rain.

8014.q: How does the white stork usually move on the ground?
8014.e: The stork walks slowly and calmly through meadows looking for prey. This makes it easier to spot frogs and insects.

8015.q: What do you call an over-the-top reaction of the immune system to harmless substances such as pollen?
8015.e: With an allergy, the immune system overreacts to substances that are actually harmless. Typical examples are hay fever or nut allergies.
8015.m: With an allergy, the immune system overreacts.

8016.q: How does a dog's hearing differ from a human's?
a: Dogs hear much higher frequencies and from further away
8016.e: Dogs' hearing is much finer than human hearing and reaches higher frequencies. They can also locate the source of sounds very precisely.

8017.q: What are fish called that migrate between the sea and fresh water, like the salmon?
8017.e: Salmon spend part of their life in the sea and part in rivers. Such fish are called migratory fish.
8017.m: Migratory fish travel between sea and river.

8018.q: What has been observed with the golden jackal in Europe in recent decades?
a: It has become a sea animal
8018.e: The golden jackal is moving from south-eastern Europe into new areas. It has also been spotted in countries where it used to be absent.
8018.m: The golden jackal is spreading in Europe.

8019.q: Where do mute swans usually sleep?
8019.e: On the water, mute swans are safe from many enemies. That is why they prefer to sleep there.
8019.m: Sleeping on the water is safe.

8020.q: Where does the edible frog often spend the winter?
a: In the mud at the bottom of the water or on land
8020.e: Many edible frogs spend the winter buried in the mud at the bottom of the water. Others spend the winter on land in frost-free hiding places.
8020.m: Edible frogs spend the winter in mud or on land.

8021.q: What colour are the great tit's wings usually?
a: Bluish grey with a white stripe
8021.e: The great tit's wings are bluish grey with a striking white stripe. You can see it well when the bird flies.
8021.m: The wings are bluish grey with a white stripe.

8022.q: How old can a barn owl get in the wild?
a: Often only two to four years
8022.e: In the wild, barn owls usually live only a few years. Harsh winters and little food make life hard for them.
8022.m: They usually live only a few years.

8023.q: What is the basic difference between weather and climate?
a: Weather is short-term, climate is the long-term average
Weather only exists in summer, climate only in winter
Weather is only about rain, climate only about wind
8023.e: Weather describes the current state of the atmosphere at a place, for example today or tomorrow. Climate is the statistical average of weather data over many decades.
8023.m: Climate is the average of many years of weather.

8024.q: The scientific name of the domestic dog is Canis lupus familiaris. Which animal is it descended from?
8024.e: Lupus is the Latin word for wolf. The domestic dog is descended from the wolf and was tamed by humans a long time ago.
8024.m: The dog is descended from the wolf.

8025.q: What colour is the common earwig usually?
8025.e: Its body is dark brown to reddish brown. This gives it good camouflage.
8025.m: It is a plain brown colour.

8026.q: How does the slow worm give birth to its young?
a: The young break out of thin egg membranes right at birth
It lays hard-shelled eggs in water
It carries the young in its mouth
It builds a nest like a bird
8026.e: The slow worm gives birth to live young in a broader sense. The eggs develop inside the mother's body, and the young are born in thin membranes, which they leave straight away.
8026.m: Slow worms give birth to live young.

8027.q: How long does a cow carry her calf before it is born?
8027.e: A cow carries her calf for about nine months, about as long as in humans. Then the calf is born.
8027.m: Calves grow for about nine months.

8028.q: How many toes does a donkey have on each foot?
8028.e: Like horses, donkeys have only one toe per foot, protected by a hard hoof. This is typical of the whole horse family.
8028.m: Donkeys walk on a single hoof.

8029.q: What special ability does the common wall lizard have when an enemy grabs it?
8029.e: If the wall lizard is grabbed by the tail, the tail breaks off on purpose. This lets the lizard itself escape.
8029.m: Shedding its tail saves its life.

8030.q: What does the okapi's coat look like?
8030.e: The short, dense coat feels velvety. It helps the okapi not to get wet quickly in the damp forest.

8031.q: What clearly sets the way the alpine salamander has young apart from the tawny owl?
a: It gives birth to live young instead of laying eggs
It lays many more eggs than the tawny owl
Both give birth to live young
It incubates its eggs in a nest
8031.e: While the tawny owl, as a bird, lays and incubates eggs, the alpine salamander gives birth to fully developed live young. That is a big difference.
8031.m: Live birth instead of laying and incubating eggs.

8032.q: Which two species does the edible frog come from as a natural cross?
a: The marsh frog and the pool frog
The tree frog and the common frog
The common toad and the natterjack toad
The agile frog and the moor frog
8032.e: The edible frog is a natural mix of the marsh frog and the pool frog. This special kind of mixing is called hybridogenesis.
8032.m: The edible frog is a mix of two water frog species.

8033.q: Where does the mole like to live best?
a: Underground in tunnels it digs itself
8033.e: The mole spends almost its whole life underground. There it digs itself a network of tunnels.

a: Alive, as a baby in the water
8034.e: Orcas are mammals, so the mother gives birth to a live baby. The baby can swim straight away.
8034.m: Orcas give birth to live young.

8035.q: How does the European garden spider sense that something has got caught in its web?
a: It sees it very clearly straight away
8035.e: The spider has fine hairs on its legs that sense the vibrations of the web. That is how it knows where something has got caught.

8036.q: What do alpacas do when they hear an unfamiliar sound?
a: They raise their heads and look closely
8036.e: Alpacas are prey animals and watch their surroundings carefully. When there is danger, they warn the herd with an alarm call.

8037.q: What can people do to help sand lizards in the garden?
a: Provide piles of stones, sandy patches or dead wood as hiding places
Cover the whole garden in tarmac
Mow the lawn down to the roots every day
8037.e: Such natural features offer warmth, hiding places and food. Many conservation projects in Switzerland rely on exactly this to help endangered species.
8037.m: Wildlife-friendly gardens help the sand lizard.

8038.q: Why is protecting nesting sites on beaches so important?
a: So that the nests are not disturbed or destroyed
Because otherwise beaches get too crowded
So that tourists can swim better
So that the turtles can smell better
8038.e: If nests are disturbed or destroyed, no new turtles can hatch. That is why many countries give special protection to important nesting beaches.

8039.q: Which animal appears on the coat of arms of the canton of Uri, whose name may come from the Latin word for aurochs?
8039.e: The black bull's head with a red nose ring has been the coat of arms of Uri since the Middle Ages. A connection with the Latin word “urus” for aurochs is suspected.
8039.m: Uri shows a bull's head on its coat of arms.

8040.q: Is the barn owl heavier or lighter than an eagle owl?
8040.e: The eagle owl is one of the largest owls and weighs much more. The barn owl is slimmer and lighter.
8040.m: The barn owl is lighter than the eagle owl.

8041.q: What do the feathers of young common ravens often look like compared to adults?
a: Much more colourful with red spots
8041.e: Young ravens have less glossy, duller feathers than adults. The typical metallic sheen develops only over time.
8041.m: Young birds look duller than adults.

8042.q: What behaviour do kestrels sometimes show along busy roads?
a: They hunt mice along the roadsides, where the grass is often kept short
They build their nests in the middle of the road
They always fly straight into car headlights
8042.e: Along roadsides the grass is often mown short, which makes it easier to hunt mice. That is why kestrels can often be seen by motorways, sitting on pylons or hovering.

8043.q: What enemies does the wild rabbit have in Switzerland?
a: Foxes, birds of prey and weasels
Roe deer, red deer and chamois
8043.e: In Switzerland, foxes, birds of prey and weasels are among the natural enemies of wild rabbits. That is why they always have to be on the lookout.
8043.m: Foxes and birds of prey hunt rabbits.

8044.q: Roughly how big is a kestrel?
a: About the size of a pigeon
About the size of a sparrow
About the size of a stork
About the size of a golden eagle
8044.e: A kestrel is around 35 centimetres long, about the size of a pigeon. It is a rather small bird of prey.

8046.q: Apart from sleeping, what other job does the meerkats' burrow do?
8046.e: It is cooler in the burrow than outside. It also offers protection from enemies and a safe place for the young.
8046.m: The burrow protects from heat and enemies.

8047.q: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe have?
a: 7, exactly as many as a human
8047.e: Even though its neck is so long, the giraffe has only seven neck vertebrae. But each one is very long.
8047.m: Giraffes have seven long neck vertebrae.

8048.q: How big can a goldfish grow if it lives in a large pond?
8048.e: In a large pond with lots of space, goldfish can grow surprisingly big, sometimes over thirty centimetres. In a small tank they usually stay small.
8048.m: Goldfish grow huge in large ponds.

8049.q: What happens when Bactrian camels have had little food for a long time and use up their humps?
a: The humps go floppy and flop to the side
8049.e: When the fat is used up, the humps go floppy. After good feeding they stand up again.
8049.m: Floppy humps show the fat has been used.

8050.q: How long does a young bearded vulture still depend on its parents after its first flight?
8050.e: Even after the young bearded vulture can fly, its parents still help feed it for a few months. Only then does it become fully independent.
8050.m: Parents help for a long time after the first flight.

8051.q: In which season does the robin's breeding season usually begin?
8051.e: In spring, when it gets warmer and there are more insects, the robin starts building its nest and breeding. That is the best time for raising young.
8051.m: The breeding season begins in spring.

8052.q: What do woodlice return to the soil when they eat leaves and droppings?
a: Nutrients that plants can take up again
8052.e: Their droppings contain nutrients that are processed further in the soil. In this way, woodlice help in nature's cycle.

8053.q: Which animal likes to hunt mosquitoes in the air?
8053.e: Bats fly at night and catch lots of mosquitoes. A single bat can eat a great many mosquitoes in one evening.

8054.q: What do young sea turtles often eat differently from adults?
a: They eat more small animals instead of plants
8054.e: While adult green sea turtles eat a lot of seagrass, the young feed more on small animals such as jellyfish or crabs. Only later do many switch to plant food.
8054.m: Young turtles often eat more animal food.

8055.q: What does the tawny owl mainly eat?
8055.e: Mice make up most of the tawny owl's food. It also eats small birds, insects and sometimes earthworms.

8057.q: What is the role of a salmon's fat reserves before its spawning migration?
a: Energy for the journey, as it hardly eats
8057.e: During the migration, salmon usually hardly eat at all. They live on the reserves they built up in the sea.
8057.m: Fat reserves give energy for the migration.

8058.q: Why should children always wear a helmet when riding a horse?
a: To protect their head if they fall
So that the horse recognises them
So that they don't get cold
8058.e: A riding helmet protects your head if you fall off the horse. This is very important when riding, because you sit quite high up.
8058.m: A helmet protects your head when riding.

8060.q: How does a seahorse snap up its prey?
a: Lightning fast with its tube-shaped snout
8060.e: Although the seahorse swims slowly, its snout can snap shut at lightning speed. That is how it catches its tiny prey in the water.
8060.m: The snout snaps shut lightning fast.

8061.q: What is the pool frog, the other parent species, usually like compared to the edible frog?
a: Smaller and with shorter back legs
Much bigger than any edible frog
8061.e: The pool frog usually stays smaller and has shorter back legs than the marsh frog and the edible frog. Even so, it is one of the two original species of the edible frog.
8061.m: The pool frog is daintier than the edible frog.

8062.q: Why do many male edible frogs often call at the same time in a loud chorus?
a: So that together their calls can be heard further away and attract females
So that they can fight each other
8062.e: When many males call at once, the overall sound gets louder and attracts females from further away. This croaking together is called chorusing.

8063.q: Which is usually heavier, a bison bull or a bison cow?
8063.e: Bulls are much bigger and stronger than cows. This is the case in many horned animals.

8064.q: What is often different about male bumblebees compared to workers?
8064.e: Male bumblebees often have slightly longer antennae than the workers. This sometimes helps tell them apart.

8065.q: What do llamas sometimes do when they feel threatened or annoyed?
8065.e: Llamas spit to defend themselves or to settle arguments. Usually they spit at other llamas.

8066.q: Why do bees from the same hive often smell similar?
a: They share a common hive scent
They only eat from one flower
They are always the same age
8066.e: Every bee colony has its own smell by which the bees recognise each other. This lets guard bees spot strange intruders.
8066.m: Every colony has its own smell.

8067.q: What role do dragonflies play in the ecosystem?
a: They keep mosquitoes and other insects in check
8067.e: Dragonflies eat lots of mosquitoes and small insects. At the same time they are food for other animals.
8067.m: As hunters, dragonflies keep insects in check.

8068.q: Which group of animals does the kangaroo belong to?
8068.e: Kangaroo mothers carry their babies in a pouch on their belly. That is why they are called marsupials.

8069.q: Why do emperor penguins often stand close together in winter?
8069.e: In icy cold, many penguins huddle very close together. That way they give each other warmth and shelter from the wind.
8069.m: Penguins huddle together against the cold.

8070.q: What sets the slow worm apart from a frog?
a: It has dry, scaly skin and lays no spawn
It has a tadpole larval stage
8070.e: Frogs are amphibians with moist skin and tadpoles. The slow worm is a reptile with scales.
8070.m: Reptiles have scales, amphibians have moist skin.

8071.q: Which order of birds does the carrion crow belong to?
8071.e: The carrion crow belongs to the perching birds, even though it is much bigger than a typical sparrow. Crows are the largest members of this order.

8072.q: What colour is the cross on the Swiss flag?
8072.e: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. It is one of the oldest flags in the world.
8072.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background.

8073.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female edible frog lay in one season?
a: Several hundred to over a thousand
8073.e: A female edible frog can lay several hundred to over a thousand eggs in one breeding season. Even so, only a few of them survive to become adult frogs.
8073.m: Females lay a great many eggs.

8075.q: What is special about the striped hyena's coat?
a: Dark stripes on a pale background
8075.e: The striped hyena has grey to yellowish fur with dark stripes across it. On its neck and back it has a mane that it can raise.
8075.m: Striped hyenas have dark stripes in their fur.

8076.q: Roughly how many species of ladybird are there worldwide?
8076.e: There are many thousands of different ladybird species around the world. They differ in colour, size and number of spots.
8076.m: There are thousands of ladybird species.

8077.q: How can a tapir breathe when it dives underwater?
8077.e: Tapirs are mammals and have lungs. When diving they hold their breath, and sometimes they even walk along the bottom.

8078.q: What does it mean that female fire salamanders release larvae instead of eggs into the water?
a: The eggs develop inside the mother's body
The eggs are buried in the sand
The father carries the eggs on his back
The eggs develop in a bird's nest
8078.e: Unlike many other amphibians, the female does not release eggs but larvae that have already hatched into the water. So the eggs develop inside the mother's body.
8078.m: Larvae are released instead of eggs.

8079.q: What do many wild reindeer do over the course of the year?
a: They stay by the same tree all year
8079.e: Wild reindeer migrate between summer and winter pastures. Some herds cover very long distances.

8080.q: Which sense is especially well developed in the tapir?
8080.e: Tapirs find their way mainly with their nose and ears. Their eyes are rather small and they don't see particularly well.
8080.m: Tapirs rely on their nose and ears.

8081.q: What does a beech marten mainly eat?
a: Mice, birds, eggs, fruit and insects
8081.e: The beech marten eats almost anything and adapts its food to the seasons. In autumn it also likes sweet fruit such as cherries.
8081.m: The beech marten eats almost anything edible.

8082.q: What is the government of a canton usually called?
a: Government Council or Council of State
8082.e: Every canton has its own government. Depending on the canton, it is called the Government Council, the Council of State or something else.
8082.m: A cantonal government is often called the Government Council.

8083.q: What colour is the fur of the edible dormouse usually?
a: Grey fur with a pale belly
8083.e: The edible dormouse usually has grey fur on its back and a paler, almost white belly. This camouflage helps it in the forest.
8083.m: Its fur is grey with a pale belly.

8084.q: What sometimes happens when a squirrel can no longer find the nuts it hid?
a: New trees can grow from the nuts
8084.e: Forgotten nuts can sprout in the ground and grow into new trees. So the squirrel even helps the forest.

8085.q: Why does the robin often sing very early in the morning?
8085.e: With its song, the robin shows other birds that this area belongs to it. It also uses its song to look for a partner.

8086.q: What does the mother rabbit use to line the nest for her young?
8086.e: The mother rabbit plucks out soft fur and lines the nest with it. There the young are nice and warm.
8086.m: The nest is lined with her own fur.

8087.q: What are the young of a fox called?
8087.e: Young foxes are called cubs or kits. They are born in spring in the fox's den.

8088.q: What does the breast of an adult peregrine falcon usually look like?
a: Pale with fine dark bars across it
8088.e: The pale breast is crossed by fine dark bars. This pattern is typical of adult peregrine falcons.

8089.q: In which unit is frequency measured, for example of sound waves or alternating current?
8089.e: Frequency tells you how often something repeats per second, for example how often a wave vibrates. The unit is named after the physicist Heinrich Hertz.

8090.q: How do many blackbirds react when a person approaches in the garden?
a: They fly off quickly with loud calls
They stay completely still and keep singing
8090.e: When someone approaches, the blackbird usually flies off quickly with a loud alarm call. This protects it from possible danger.
8090.m: Blackbirds often flee calling when in danger.

8091.q: What happens to a brown bear's heart rate during its winter rest?
a: It stays exactly the same as in summer
8091.e: During winter rest, the bear's heart rate drops sharply to save energy. Even so, it can quickly become active again if disturbed.
8091.m: In winter rest the bear's heart beats more slowly.

8092.q: What does a ladybird larva look like?
a: Long, dark and a bit like a little crocodile
Soft and woolly like a caterpillar
8092.e: The larva has no spots but is long and dark, often with small orange patches. It looks completely different from the later beetle.

8093.q: Can a common buzzard briefly stay in one spot in the air like a kestrel?
a: Yes, occasionally, but not as skilfully as the kestrel
No, it can't fly at all
Yes, it hovers all day without stopping
8093.e: The common buzzard can occasionally hover briefly, almost flying on the spot, but it is less skilled at it than the kestrel. Usually it prefers to watch from a perch.
8093.m: It can hover, but rarely does.

8094.q: Where do wild budgerigars like to live best?
8094.e: Wild budgerigars like open, dry grassland with bushes. There they find seeds to eat.

8095.q: What is it called when a herd of bison runs off in panic?
8095.e: The word stampede comes from Spanish and describes a wild flight. The whole herd runs together.
8095.m: A panicked mass flight is called a stampede.

8096.q: In which country do bonobos live in the wild?
a: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo
8096.e: Bonobos live only in the rainforest of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Africa. An important protected area is Salonga National Park.
8096.m: Bonobos live only in the Congo.

8097.q: What shape does the shell of a Roman snail show if you look closely?
8097.e: The Roman snail's shell grows in a beautiful spiral shape. The bigger the snail gets, the bigger the spiral becomes.
8097.m: The shell grows in a spiral.

8098.q: What is the difference between a series circuit and a parallel circuit?
a: In a series circuit the current has only one path, in a parallel circuit several paths
Both are built in exactly the same way
There is no current in a series circuit
8098.e: In a series circuit all the components are connected one after another; if one fails, the whole circuit goes off. In a parallel circuit components have their own paths, so they work independently of each other.
8098.m: A series circuit has one path, a parallel circuit several.

8099.e: Only female wasps have a sting. The male wasps, also called drones, therefore cannot sting.

8100.q: Are you allowed to keep a robin as a pet at home?
a: No, it is a protected wild bird
Yes, but only in a cage
8100.e: Because the robin is a protected wild bird, you are not allowed to catch it and keep it at home. It should live freely in nature.

8102.q: Where does the lowland tapir live?
8102.e: The lowland tapir is found in large parts of South America east of the Andes. It lives in forests and wetlands.
8102.m: Lowland tapirs live in South America.

8103.q: What does the blackbird build its nest from?
8103.e: For its nest, the blackbird collects grass, thin twigs and some mud. This makes the nest firm and cup-shaped.
8103.m: The blackbird's nest is made of grass and mud.

8105.q: Where do giraffe mothers often hide their calves in the first weeks?
a: In tall grass while they go off to feed
In the water of a lake
8105.e: In the first weeks, the calf often lies well hidden in tall grass or bushes. The mother feeds nearby and keeps coming back to suckle it.
8105.m: Giraffe calves hide in tall grass.

8106.q: The sea trout is the same species as the brown trout. What does it do differently?
a: It migrates to the sea and returns to rivers to spawn
It only lives in mountain lakes
8106.e: The sea trout feeds in the sea and grows bigger there. To spawn, it swims into rivers and streams.
8106.m: Sea trout spawn in fresh water.

8108.q: What kind of water does a trout absolutely need to survive?
a: Chlorinated water from the swimming pool
8108.e: Trout need lots of oxygen in the water to breathe well. That is why they prefer to live in fresh, flowing water.

8109.q: What are animals called that eat both meat and plants?
8109.e: Omnivores such as bears or wild boar eat both plant and animal food. Humans are omnivores too.

8110.q: How does the praying mantis usually hunt?
a: It lies in wait without moving and then strikes
It chases its prey for hours
8110.e: The praying mantis often sits completely still for a long time. When prey comes close enough, it grabs it at lightning speed.
8110.m: As an ambush hunter, the mantis waits still and then strikes.

8111.q: Up to what altitude above sea level is the European tree frog still found in Switzerland?
8111.e: In Switzerland, tree frogs are found mainly at lower altitudes, in some places up to around 1,000 metres. They are absent from the high Alpine regions.

8112.q: Which animal sits on a cactus in the centre of the Mexican coat of arms?
8112.e: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle sitting on a cactus and eating a snake. It goes back to an Aztec founding legend.
8112.m: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle with a snake.

8113.q: Where do jackals usually give birth to their pups?
a: In an earth burrow or a cave
8113.e: Jackals often use burrows in the ground as a place to give birth. There the pups are protected from weather and enemies.
8113.m: The pups grow up in a burrow.

8114.q: Which small animal is a close relative of the edible dormouse and also lives in Switzerland?
8114.e: The edible dormouse and the hazel dormouse both belong to the dormouse family. The hazel dormouse is smaller, has orange-brown fur and also hibernates for a long time.
8114.m: The hazel dormouse is related to the edible dormouse.

8115.q: Which country has the cockerel as a well-known national symbol, the “Gallic rooster”?
8115.e: The “Gallic rooster” is an old symbol of France. You can see it, for example, at sports events as a sign of the French team.

8116.q: What is the pattern on the ring-tailed lemur's tail?
8116.e: The tail has striking black and white rings. That is where the ring-tailed lemur gets its name.
8116.m: The ring-tailed lemur has a ringed tail.

8117.q: How often does the common raven usually use its nest?
a: It is often repaired and added to over several years
Only for a single brood, then never again
Only for a few hours a day
It builds a brand new nest every day
8117.e: Once built, a raven's nest is often used again for years and repaired when needed. This saves energy in the next breeding season.
8117.m: Nests are often reused for years.

8119.q: At what age can young barn swallows usually breed themselves?
a: Usually in their first year of life
Only when they are 20 years old
8119.e: Barn swallows are already able to breed in their first year of life. This is important because their lifespan is rather short anyway.
8119.m: Able to breed in their first year.

8120.q: What do young martens feed on before they eat solid food?
8120.e: Like other mammals, young martens first drink their mother's milk. Only after a few weeks do they start eating solid food such as small prey.
8120.m: Young martens drink their mother's milk first.

8121.q: Which senses help the wels catfish most in murky water?
8121.e: The wels catfish has small eyes and sees poorly. But its barbels and skin are very good at sensing touch and taste.
8121.m: The wels catfish feels its way through the water.

8122.q: On which continents is the red fox naturally common?
a: In large parts of Europe, Asia and North America
Only on a small island in the Pacific
8122.e: The red fox is one of the most widespread predators in the world and lives in large parts of Europe, Asia and North America. Its adaptability makes it very successful.
8122.m: The fox lives on many continents.

8123.q: What does a giraffe like to eat best?
8123.e: Giraffes eat only plants and especially like the leaves of acacias. With their long tongue they skilfully pluck the leaves from between the thorns.

8124.q: When does a red deer stag normally shed its old antlers?
a: Never, it keeps them for ever
8124.e: Towards the end of winter or in spring, the old antlers fall off. Straight afterwards, new ones start to grow.
8124.m: The antlers fall off in spring.

a: The period of time an elected parliament or government is in office
The length of a parliamentary sitting
8125.e: At federal level, a legislative period lasts four years. After that there are elections again.
8125.m: A legislative period is the parliament's term of office.

8126.q: How does the tawny owl usually eat a small mouse?
a: It chews it for a long time with its teeth
It first lets it soften in water
8126.e: The tawny owl usually swallows small prey such as mice whole. It later coughs up the bones and hair as a pellet.
8126.m: Tawny owls swallow small prey whole.

8127.q: A horse's eyes are on the sides of its head. Where can it see with them?
8127.e: Because their eyes are on the sides of the head, horses can see almost all of their surroundings. However, they see poorly right in front of and behind them.
8127.m: Horses see almost all the way round.

8128.q: How exactly does the Roman snail's foot move when it crawls?
8128.e: The snail's foot moves in fine waves from back to front. That is how it pushes itself forward bit by bit.
8128.m: Wave movements push the snail forwards.

8129.q: Which rhinoceros species is the smallest of all?
8129.e: The Sumatran rhino is the smallest of the five rhino species. It lives in dense forests in Asia and has some hair.
8129.m: The Sumatran rhino is the smallest.

8130.q: What is important so that a goldfish pond doesn't get too warm for the fish in summer?
a: Enough shade, for example from plants
Filling it with hot tap water
8130.e: When a pond gets too warm in summer, the water holds less oxygen and the fish suffer. Shade, for example from water lily leaves, helps keep the water cooler.
8130.m: Shade keeps the pond cooler in summer.

8131.q: What does it usually mean when a horse lays its ears back flat?
8131.e: Ears laid back often show that a horse feels uncomfortable or irritated. You should be careful then.
8131.m: Ears laid back show a bad mood.

8132.q: Roughly how much does a female red kite weigh?
8132.e: Female red kites are a little heavier than males and weigh just over a kilogram on average. This is typical of many birds of prey.
8132.m: A female red kite weighs just over a kilo.

8133.q: What is the development of the grasshopper called, in which there is no pupal stage?
8133.e: In grasshoppers, the young already look almost like the adults. They simply grow by shedding their skin, without becoming pupae.
8133.m: The nymph already looks almost like an adult.

8134.q: What is one difference between an elk (moose) and a reindeer?
a: The elk only lives in Africa
8134.e: Elk are much bigger and heavier than reindeer. Reindeer also often live in herds.

8135.q: Why is the okapi hard for researchers to observe?
a: It lives shyly in dense forest
8135.e: Okapis are shy and well camouflaged in the dense rainforest. That is why comparatively little is known about them.
8135.m: Okapis are shy and well hidden.

8136.q: What does the slow worm do in winter?
a: It rests through the winter in a frost-free hiding place
It stays as active as in summer
8136.e: As a cold-blooded animal, it becomes stiff in the cold. It looks for frost-free hiding places, for example in the ground or under stones.
8136.m: In winter it rests hidden from the frost.

8137.q: A rabbit is lying stretched out and calm in its enclosure. How does it usually feel?
a: It is relaxed and feels safe
It wants to play straight away
8137.e: When a rabbit lies stretched out and calm, it feels comfortable and safe. A frightened rabbit, on the other hand, crouches down small.
8137.m: Lying stretched out shows the rabbit is relaxed.

8138.q: What is the difference between the active and the passive right to vote?
a: Active means being allowed to vote, passive means being allowed to be elected
Active means only voting on issues, passive means only electing
8138.e: With the active right to vote, you may cast a vote yourself. With the passive right, you may stand for election yourself.

8139.q: Why doesn't a seahorse like to swim in strong currents?
a: Because it is a weak swimmer and prefers to hold on
Because it is afraid of water
8139.e: Because seahorses swim very slowly, a strong current would simply carry them away. That is why they prefer to hold on to plants with their tail.
8139.m: Better to hold on than swim against the current.

8140.q: What does an orca mainly eat?
a: Fish, seals and other sea animals
8140.e: The orca is a hunter and eats, for example, fish, seals and even other whales. It is a carnivore.

8141.q: How are a starfish's arms arranged?
a: Around a centre, like a star
Two at the front and two at the back
8141.e: A starfish's arms all start from the centre, like the rays of a star. That is why it is called a starfish.
8141.m: Starfish arms spread out from the centre.

8142.q: What is the best way to tell a jaguar's coat from a leopard's?
a: The rosettes usually have spots inside
8142.e: In the jaguar, the rosettes are usually bigger and often contain spots. In the leopard, the rosettes are smaller and usually have no spots inside.
8142.m: Jaguar rosettes often have spots inside.

8143.q: Where do praying mantises mainly live around the world?
a: In warm regions, especially the tropics
8143.e: Most species live in the tropics and subtropics. Only a few are found in temperate areas.

8144.q: How can you tell a stoat from a least weasel?
a: By the black tip of its tail
By its fur colour in summer
8144.e: The least weasel has no black tail tip and is also smaller than the stoat. This feature helps you recognise them in nature.
8144.m: A black tail tip marks the stoat.

8145.q: How loud can a European tree frog's call be?
a: In calm weather it can often be heard kilometres away
8145.e: The mating call of tree frogs is surprisingly loud and carries very far in still weather. Whole choruses of calling males can often be heard from a long way off.

8146.q: Which statement about the Persian leopard is true?
a: It lives mainly in the Caucasus and Iran
It only lives in South America
It lives at the North Pole
8146.e: The Persian leopard is a subspecies found in Western Asia, for example in Iran and the Caucasus. It is one of the biggest subspecies.
8146.m: The Persian leopard lives in Western Asia.

8147.q: What are the little turtles called shortly after hatching?
8147.e: The tiny turtles that have just hatched from the egg are called hatchlings. They set off for the sea straight away.
8147.m: Freshly hatched turtles are called hatchlings.

8148.q: In which European country are there still wild forest reindeer?
8148.e: In Europe, wild forest reindeer live mainly in Finland and Russia. There are no wild reindeer in Switzerland.
8148.m: Wild reindeer live in the far north.

8149.q: What do the scales of a European perch feel like?
a: Rough, because they have tiny teeth on the edge
Soft and slimy, with no scales at all
As big as coins and completely smooth
8149.e: The perch has ctenoid scales with fine little teeth on the edge. That is why its skin feels quite rough.
8149.m: Toothed scales make the perch rough.

8150.q: What does an adult edible frog mainly eat?
a: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates
8150.e: Adult edible frogs are carnivores and hunt insects, spiders, worms and other small animals. Sometimes they even catch small vertebrates.
8150.m: Edible frogs eat small insects and spiders.

8151.q: Why does the adder often bask on stones?
a: It wants to take in vitamins from stones
8151.e: Its body temperature depends on its surroundings. By basking in the sun it becomes active and can hunt and digest.
8151.m: Cold-blooded animals soak up the sun's warmth.

8153.q: How does the cuckoo's flight differ from a pigeon's?
a: With its pointed wings it looks more like a falcon
It flies much more slowly than a snail
8153.e: The cuckoo has pointed wings and a long tail, which makes it look like a small falcon in flight. Some host birds mistake it for a dangerous bird of prey.
8153.m: A flying cuckoo looks like a falcon.

8154.q: What does a polar bear do to cool down or keep clean?
a: It just shakes itself dry without snow
8154.e: Polar bears like to roll in the snow to clean their fur and cool down. This also keeps their fur well insulating.
8154.m: The polar bear rolls in the snow.

8155.q: How can you often tell which species a ladybird belongs to?
a: By the number and pattern of its spots
By the smell of its feet
By the size of its eyes
By the colour of its antennae
8155.e: Different ladybird species have different numbers of spots and patterns on their wing cases. This helps experts tell the species apart.
8155.m: Spot patterns give away the species.

8156.q: How many toes does a rhinoceros have on each foot?
8156.e: A rhino has three toes on each foot, covered with small hooves. You can see this clearly in its footprints.
8156.m: Rhinos have three toes per foot.

8157.q: What colour are the eyes of adult kestrels usually?
8157.e: The kestrel's eyes are dark brown and very large for the size of its head. These big eyes help it spot prey from far away.

8158.q: Which animal is the polar bear's closest relative?
8158.e: The polar bear is descended from brown bears and is closely related to them. Both belong to the bear family.
8158.m: The brown bear is the closest relative.

8159.q: What role did the hamadryas baboon play in ancient Egypt?
a: It was considered a sacred animal
It was banned as a pet
It was seen only as a pest
8159.e: In ancient Egypt, the hamadryas baboon was linked with the god Thoth and worshipped. It appears in pictures and has been found as mummies.
8159.m: In ancient Egypt it was sacred.

a: A place where people who have fled live for a while
A holiday camp for school classes
8160.e: People who have fled from war or danger find a roof over their heads, food and help from a doctor in a refugee camp.
8160.m: Refugee camps offer protection from danger.

8161.q: What kind of weather do donkeys particularly dislike?
8161.e: Donkeys don't have water-repellent coats like horses and get wet more quickly in the rain. That is why they need a dry shelter.

8162.q: What are the long threads around the mouth of the wels catfish called?
8162.e: The wels catfish has six barbels, two long ones on the upper jaw and four short ones on the lower jaw. It uses them to feel and taste its surroundings.

8163.q: What threatens the little turtles most just after they hatch?
a: Predators such as crabs and birds
Weather that is too cold in summer
8163.e: On the short way from the nest to the water there are many dangers. Sadly, crabs, birds and other animals eat many of the tiny hatchlings.
8163.m: Crabs and birds hunt the hatchlings.

8164.q: How does the beech marten's way of life in towns differ from that in the countryside?
a: In towns it often uses lofts and cars as shelter
In towns it lives only in water
In the countryside it eats only fish
8164.e: In towns and villages, the beech marten adapts and uses buildings and vehicles as shelter. In the countryside it tends to find natural hiding places such as rock crevices.
8164.m: Beech martens adapt easily to towns and villages.

8165.q: What colour are the white stork's feathers usually?
8165.e: The white stork has white feathers, only the wing tips are black. This makes it easy to recognise in the sky.

8166.q: Do wild rabbits usually live alone or in groups?
8166.e: Wild rabbits live sociably together in colonies with many other rabbits. This way they can warn each other of enemies more easily.

8167.q: On which famous building in Basel are peregrine falcons known to breed?
8167.e: A pair of peregrine falcons has been breeding successfully on Basel Minster for years. The brood is often watched there with a camera.
8167.m: Basel Minster is a falcon nesting site.

8168.q: What is special about the beaver's back feet for swimming?
